findings.where: Title-block nav bar, the logo cell, on desktop and phone
findings.fault: The MMM Infra logo is recoloured. The arches and the 'MMM INFRA' wordmark are white, not the logo grey #404040 and logo blue #0070C0. Mark does not hold a white (reversed) version of his logo, and the tile does not say that one is proposed. It shows the white logo as if it were simply his logo on this ground.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who has said his logo stays. He would see his blue wordmark gone without being asked. The layout round would also inherit a logo version the client never approved.

findings.where: Palette section: the six swatches (Diazo blue, Linework, Sodium amber, Note blue, Table, Amber ink)
findings.fault: The palette leaves out Mark's two logo colours, logo blue #0070C0 and logo grey #404040. Neither is listed as a colour with a job or as 'logo only', and the diazo blue ground is never shown next to them. The palette is built as if the logo had no colours of its own.
findings.who_objects: Mark, and the layout round. Neither can tell from the tile how the logo's own blue sits beside diazo blue, or whether it ever appears at all.

findings.where: Article specimen: the post title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law', against the Type pair note and the name 'MARK M. MOSELEY'
findings.fault: The tile's own type note says headings are set in ExtraBold capitals, tracked wide. The article heading is in mixed case with no tracking. The name heading and every section label follow the note, so the one heading a post will use most breaks it.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, and the layout round. When she adds a post she has two rules to choose from, and the tile shows both.

findings.where: Dates and numbers in the article specimen: the meta line 'MMM Infra Blog No. 8 • 18 September 2024' and the attachment line 'Lecture • 2026-04-23 · PDF'
findings.fault: Dates and numbers are treated two ways. The tile says Overpass Mono is for drawing numbers and dates. The attachment's date is mono and written as a numeric ISO date, but the post's date and the blog number are in the sans and written out in words. One meta line also mixes two separators: '•' and '·'.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who copies whichever line she sees first, and readers, who meet two styles of date one line apart.

findings.where: Sodium amber: the hatched third bay of the hero drawing and the 'WRITE TO MARK' button. The palette swatch is labelled 'daylight in the drawing, and the one action'
findings.fault: One accent colour has two jobs. On the first screen the same amber marks a decorative part of the drawing and the only action. The action's colour no longer means 'act here', and the hatch competes with the button for the eye.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding whether to get in touch: the amber in the drawing looks as live as the button. The layout round also gets no rule for where amber may go.

findings.where: Portrait placeholder (desktop and phone); the Texture panel on phone
findings.fault: Some frames break the column's left edge. The portrait's outer frame sits about 6 px outside the line the section labels and rules follow, on desktop and on phone. On phone, the 'EARTH HATCH' label and the hatch swatch sit flush against the Texture box's left border with no inset, but they have an inset on desktop.
findings.who_objects: Mark, or anyone used to engineering drawings, where frames register exactly to the sheet. On a look built on drawing-sheet precision, small misalignments look careless.

findings.where: Portrait placeholder label 'PHOTOGRAPH OF MARK TO / COME' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The tracked capitals wrap so that 'COME' is left alone on the second line, which breaks the phrase awkwardly in a short label.
findings.who_objects: Mark, reviewing the tile: the label looks unfinished.
